Joseph Smith. Eighteen oh five to eighteen forty-four. The founding prophet of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints, known as Mormonism, a uniquely American religious movement that emerged in early nineteenth-century New York. Through his claimed visions and revelations, he established a faith that combines Christian theology with new scriptural texts and distinctive practices. Joseph Smith was born in Vermont and raised in upstate New York during a period of intense religious revival known as the Second Great Awakening. At age fourteen, he reported a vision of God and Jesus Christ instructing him that existing Christian denominations had fallen into error, initiating his prophetic mission. He claimed to have found golden plates inscribed with ancient American history, which he translated as the Book of Mormon, published in eighteen thirty as Mormonism's central scripture. The Book of Mormon claims to be a history of pre-Columbian American peoples and their encounters with Jesus Christ after his resurrection, fundamentally expanding Christian cosmology. He founded the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints in eighteen thirty, attracting thousands of followers and establishing communities in Ohio, Missouri, and Illinois. Smith taught that God continues to reveal truth through living prophets, establishing continuous revelation as a core Latter-day Saint principle distinct from mainstream Christianity. He practiced polygamy, or plural marriage, a teaching that became central to early Mormonism and caused both internal controversy and violent external opposition. He was killed by a mob in Carthage, Illinois, in eighteen forty-four, becoming a martyr figure whose death cemented his prophetic authority in Latter-day Saint tradition.
